full_judgment:
2. Md. Ismail, the predecessor of the appellants filed the above suit for ejectment of Ahammad Hussain, the predecessor of defendant respondents, from the suit premises contending, inter alia, that Ahammad Hussain, the original defendant was a monthly tenant in the suit premises, a portion of 13 Larmini Street, Wari, Dhaka, under the former owner of the premises on the basis of an agreement dated 7.1.81 at a monthly rental of Tk. 795/- excluding WASA charge of Tk.60/- to be paid by the defendant within 7th day of every English calendar month; the plaintiff having purchased the land and building situated at 13 Larmini Street, Wari, Dhaka including the suit premises, served letter of attornment on the defendant on 11.11.85; the defendant paid rent to the plaintiff for the month of December, 1985 and then inspite of repeated demands neither entered into a new agreement with the plaintiff nor paid him the rent as well as the WASA charges of the subsequent months; meanwhile the defendant filed House Rent Case No. 96 of 1986 stating that on 6.1.86 he remitted the rent by postal money order but the plaintiff having refused to accept the same the said postal money order returned back undelivered on 25.1.1986; the addresses of the plaintiff is 13, Larmini Street, Wari, Dhaka but that defendant having remitted the rent at 9/H, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka, which is not the address of - the plaintiff, the above remittance is not legal and valid and so the defendant became a defaulter; the defendant also defaulted in paying the WASA charges; further the defendant by publishing an advertisement in the daily Ittefaq on 6.10.87 for letting out a portion of 200 cubits from the suit premises also violated the provision of clause 3(b) of the agreement dated 7.1.1981; the plaintiff on 15.5.1986 issued notice to the defendant under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act terminating the tenancy with the end of the month of June, 1986 but the defendant, inspite of receipt of the same, did not vacate the suit premises and hence the suit. The defendant contested the suit filing written statement contending, inter alia, that the defendant had been a tenant in the suit premises since 1971 and paid rent to the earlier owner and on the basis of letter of attornmant also paid rent to the plaintiff upon December, 1985; the defendant, on 6.1.86, also tendered rent for the month of January, 1986 but the plaintiff having refused to accept the same the defendant by money order dated 6.1.86 sent the rent for the month of January, 1986 to the plaintiff at 9/H, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka as the address of 13 Lermini Street, Wari was not known to him and the plaintiff having refused to accept the said money order the same was returned back to the defendant undelivered; then within 15 days thereof the defendant filed House Rent Case No. 56 of 1986 and deposited the rent therein regularly; a friend of the defendant using his name and address published advertisement in the newspaper on 6.10.87 for subletting but in fact there was no sub-letting; the bathroom and latrine of the rented premises, which was situated in the ground floor, was demolished by the former owner and so the plaintiff waived WASA charges from the tenant of the ground floor; the suit premises is not needed by the plaintiff for his bonafide requirement and the defendant is also not a defaulter and there was no sub-letting of the suit premises. The trial court, after hearing, decreed the suit Then defendant having not vacated the suit premises the plaintiff filed Title Execution Case No.3 of 1991 and on the other hand the defendant preferred Title Appeal No.3 of 1991. After hearing, the learned Additional District Judge dismissed the above appeal. The defendant then moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 2997 of 1997 but since at the time of hearing of the said Rule on 9.12.98 none appeared for the defendant, the High Court Division discharged the Rule for default, then the plaintiff got delivery of possession of the suit premises through Court on 11.2.2000 in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1991. Thereafter on 24.2.2000 the substituted defendant/respondents, as legal heirs of the defendant, filed application before the High Court Division for restoration of the above Rule which was earlier discharged on 9.12.1998 and after hearing the High Court Division restored the Rule to its file and number. Then, after hearing, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute holding that the defendant on 6.1.1986 tendered to the plaintiff the rent for the month of January, 1986 by money order and the evidence on record shows that the said money order having not been accepted by the plaintiff returned to the defendant and then the defendant started House Rent Case No. 56 of 1986 and had been depositing the rent therein since January, 1986; the defendant is not a defaulter and further no illegality or irregularity could also be pointed out by the learned advocate appearing for the plaintiff/opposite party before the High Court Division. 

 3. Leave was granted on the submissions that the tenant was defaulter as he sent the rent by postal money order in the wrong address of the plaintiff prior to the filing of the said house rent control case and that under section 18 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance it is obligatory on the part of a tenant to remit by postal money order to the address of the landlord and if it is not done a landlord shall not be deemed to have refused to accept the rent. 

 4. The learned counsel for the appellants submits that the defendant having not remitted the postal money order to the address of the plaintiff which is 13 Larmini Street, Wari, Dhaka and the same having sent to a place which is not the address of the plaintiff, in view of the provision of sub section (5) of section 18 of the House Rent Control Ordinance it cannot be said that the plaintiff refused to accept the rent from the tenant and, as such, the deposit of rent to the House Rent Controller is not a legal and valid deposit and so the finding of the High Court Division that "the defendant is not a defaulter" is erroneous as after the purchase of the suit premises from the former landlord of the defendant, both the plaintiff and the above former landlord served letter of attornment to the defendant on 17.11.85 wherein the address of the plaintiff was shown at 13 Larmini Street, Wari, Dhaka and upon receipt of the said letter of attornment the defendant paid rent to the plaintiff for the month of December 1985 and inspite of that instead of paying the rent for the month of January, 1986 the defendant remitted the rent by postal money order at 9/H, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka which is not the address of the plaintiff and accordingly the respondents are not entitled to get benefit of section 18 of the Premises and Rent Control Ordinance. 

 5. The learned counsel appearing for the respondent submits that the High Court Division found that the defendant is not a defaulter and he sent the rent by postal money order wherein the address of the plaintiff has been shown at 9-H, Motijheel Commercial Area and further the rent deposited before the House Rent Controller has been withdrawn by the plaintiff without raising any objection as to the correctness of his address as showed therein and so the claim of the plaintiff that house rent has not been sent in proper address is no longer tenable and further this contention regarding the correctness of the address of the plaintiff having not been raised either before the trial court or in the appellate Court or in the High Court Division, the plaintiff cannot be allowed to raise it before this Division. 

 6. As it appears that trial court found that the defendant is defaulter because he paid the rent for the month of January 1986 but did not pay the WASA charges as provided in clause 3(b) of the lease agreement Ext. 1. The appellate Court on the other hand found that no agreement for rent was entered by the plaintiff and the defendant and so there was no relationship of land-lord and tenant between them and so the defendant had no obligation to pay the rent of the month of January 1986 to the plaintiff. However the High Court Division found that Ext.1 created lease but clause 3(b) of the same having provided that WASA bill has to be paid within the month along with rent non-payment of the same along with monthly rent, non-payment of WASA bill along with the rent of the month of January 1986 can not be a ground for treating the defendant as defaulter; further the plaintiff after purchase of the suit premises accepted the defendant as a tenant and received the rent from him for the month of December, 1985 subject to a new agreement; the case of the defendant is that he paid rent for the month of January 1986 on 06.01.86 and the plaintiff having refused to accept the rent he sent the rent by money order to the plaintiff and the evidence on record shows that the above money order being not accepted by the plaintiff returned back to the defendant and then the defendant started House Rent Case No: 56 of 1986 and had been depositing the rent there since January, 1986 and the plaintiff also had been withdrawing the said rent. 

 7. However as it appears from the contents of Ext.3, the attornment letter filed by the plaintiff, below the signatures of the plaintiff as well as Mr. Hasan Faruque, the vendor of the plaintiff, their addresses had been written in separate ink. The defendant asserted that in Ext. Kha, the attornment letter received by him, the residential address of the plaintiff has not been mentioned. At the time of hearing, the defendant respondent along with supplementary affidavit, filed similar allotment letters sent to other tenants of the premises and also the copy of the passport of the plaintiff respondent. As it appears in the attornment letters filed by the plaintiff, Ext.3, after the signature of the plaintiff, the address of the plaintiff has been shown as 13, Larmini Street in separate handwriting and also in different ink and further the signature of the plaintiff in the above attornment letter also differ from the signature of the plaintiff in the passport which was issued on 05.03.1989. Further it also appears that the attornment letter which the defendant filed i.e. Ext. Kha, contains no such residential address of the plaintiff and merely showed official address at 9/H Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka and further the signature of the plaintiff on the same also differs from his other signatures. 

 8. It also appears that in paragraph 6 of the written statement, the defendant categorically stated that the plaintiff did not inform him his address at 13 Larmini Street. As it appears inspite of the above specific assertion in the written statement and inspite of filing of Ext. Kha the witnesses of the plaintiff in their deposition did not assert that the defendant knew that the address of the plaintiff was 12 Larmini Street and moreover though the defendant No.1 examined himself as D.W.1 and proved Ext. Kha but there was no endeavor from the side of the plaintiff to cross examine D.W.1 to the effect that he knew that the address of the plaintiff was 12 Larmini Street specifically when issue was also framed as to whether the defendant, in compliance of section 18(5) of the Premises and Rent Control Ordinance, sent the rent for the month of January 1986 to the correct address of the plaintiff. As it appears the plaintiff having not raised this point the trial court as well as the appellate court did not advert this point.
